contracts.commit_point: The HTTP POST with JSON-RPC method 'tools/call' to K8S_MCP_URL issued by _post_mcp/mcp_call_tool when a guarded tool function runs (supervisor/agents.py:84-109); the resulting Kubernetes mutation is performed by the MCP server outside the supplied source.
contracts.declared_mechanism: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on=hitl_policy, description_prefix='Tool execution pending approval') registered in create_agent for the operations agent, with per-tool interrupt flags set True for the five mutating tools and False for read-only tools (supervisor/agents.py:353-373); enforced end-to-end by the FastAPI approval loop that stores pending interrupts (supervisor/app.py:107-118), parses approve/reject decisions against allowed_decisions (supervisor/app.py:73-93, 147-179), and resumes the interrupted execution only via agent.invoke(Command(resume={'decisions': decisions_payload})) after a valid parsed decision (supervisor/app.py:170-185).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A mutating operations-agent tool call (create_pod, delete_pod, scale_deployment, restart_rollout, patch_resource) executing, or being dispatched via the tools/call POST to the K8s MCP server, without a prior explicit human approval decision for that specific interrupted call.
pending_binding_information: Whether HumanInTheLoopMiddleware's interrupt guarantees the guarded tool function body (and thus the tools/call POST) never executes before Command(resume) is delivered — middleware implementation not supplied.

Whether approvals on /run are authenticated or attributed to an authorized human; no authentication is visible in the supplied app.py, so any client posting to a thread with a pending interrupt can supply the decision.
Whether the in-memory PENDING_INTERRUPTS dict and InMemorySaver checkpointer preserve the approval hold across process restarts — restart behavior not determinable from supplied source.
Whether the K8s MCP server applies its own authorization to tools/call requests — server source not supplied.

Whether the exec_shell-based mutating tools (create_pod, restart_rollout, patch_resource) and the direct MCP calls (delete_pod, scale_deployment) have identical server-side execution guarantees at the MCP server — not observable in supplied source.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of the operations agent's mutating Kubernetes tools: create_pod (kubectl run via exec_shell), delete_pod (direct MCP tool call), scale_deployment (direct MCP tool call), restart_rollout (kubectl rollout restart via exec_shell), and patch_resource (kubectl patch via exec_shell).
contracts.protected_resource: Kubernetes cluster state (pods, deployments, and other patchable resources in target namespaces) reached through the K8s MCP server at K8S_MCP_URL.
contracts.protection_obligation: Mutating Kubernetes tool calls issued by the operations agent (create_pod, delete_pod, scale_deployment, restart_rollout, patch_resource) must be interrupted by the registered HumanInTheLoopMiddleware and must not be dispatched for execution (the tools/call POST to the K8s MCP server) until an explicit human approve decision is parsed and the interrupted graph is resumed via Command(resume=...).
scope_limits: Read-only operations tools (list_namespaces, list_pods, describe_resource) are explicitly excluded from interruption (hitl_policy values False at supervisor/agents.py:360-362).

Diagnostics-path tools bypass the operations agent and its HITL middleware entirely, including the arbitrary-command exec_shell binding (supervisor/agents.py:222) and the read-only kubectl get invocation in analysis_node (supervisor/agents.py:313); they are outside this contract.

The keyword-based mitigation execution gate (supervisor/agents.py:331-332, 422-425) is a separate, weaker keyword check and is not part of the declared HITL mechanism; mitigation execution still routes through the operations agent (supervisor/agents.py:339-350), where the middleware applies.

The contract binds only up to the tools/call POST dispatch from the supervisor process; the Kubernetes mutation performed by the MCP server occurs outside the supplied source and cannot be contracted here.
Semantics of the HumanInTheLoopMiddleware library (whether an interrupt guarantees the tool body never runs before resume) are library internals not present in the supplied source.

missing_information: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware library implementation is not supplied, so whether a registered interrupt prevents the tool function body (and its tools/call POST) from executing before Command(resume) cannot be confirmed from source.
The K8s MCP server implementation is not supplied; server-side authorization or re-validation of mutating tools/call requests is unknown.
The /run endpoint in supervisor/app.py shows no authentication or authorization on approval decisions; whether approvals must come from an identified, authorized human is unsupported.
Persistence semantics of PENDING_INTERRUPTS and the InMemorySaver checkpointer across restarts are not determinable from supplied source.

The original adjective in supervisor/prompts.py line 35 is redacted ('Any <REDACTED> action requires explicit approval'), so the prompt-level policy's intended coverage (e.g., whether it extends to arbitrary diagnostics exec_shell commands) cannot be established.
